summary: Patch resolves the boolean-X TypeError by casting X to float, but places the cast inside `_huber_loss_and_gradient`, which the L-BFGS optimizer calls repeatedly, so X is re-copied to float64 on every iteration. Correct fix belongs in `fit` via `check_X_y(..., dtype=[np.float64, np.float32])`, matching `LinearRegression`.

issues.description: `X = X.astype(float)` runs inside the loss/gradient function called once per optimizer iteration, allocating a fresh float64 copy of X each call. Avoidable repeated allocation; should cast once in `fit`.

Wrong location for the fix. sklearn idiom is to validate/coerce dtype in `fit` via `check_X_y`/`check_array`; coercing deep inside the numeric kernel is fragile and inconsistent with other estimators.
`astype(float)` forces float64, silently upcasting a float32 X (extra memory, lost dtype intent) rather than preserving supported float dtypes as check_X_y dtype list would.
Trailing whitespace on the blank comment line and inline coercion deviate from repo style/validation conventions.
